title: Apocalypse: The Hunger — Tackling sprite animation consistency & procedural city generation with generative assets
author: Fickle_Capital6796
selftext:
Sharing some progress on my upcoming open-world tactical deckbuilder, **Apocalypse: The Hunger**.

A lot of projects in the AI space stick strictly to static portraits, visual novels, or UI skins because multi-frame animation usually warps character silhouettes and creates erratic frame jumps. For this project, I wanted to focus on two core systems:

* **Manual Sprite Animation Loop:** The side-by-side shot shows the actual idle/movement loop. Instead of relying on full-sequence generation (which tends to lose coherence), I engineered a modular keyframe pipeline using generative slices to maintain volume, clean edge tracking, and silhouette consistency.
* **Procedural City Engine:** The entire environment runs on a procedural layout stack that handles dynamic collision grids, sector zoning, and tile mapping, feeding live into the combat logs and minimap pathing.
* **HD Enhancer Pipeline:** To remove the flat, washed-out artifacts common with raw generative outputs, every asset was run through a custom-built contrast and dynamic lighting enhancer tool prior to engine import.

Can you spot the difference from the post-processing enhancer in the screenshot? Would love to hear feedback on the grid readability and UI layout.
